newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Pao de Acucar to invest $479.4 mln.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Pao de Acucar to invest $479.4 mln.

text.p: Brazilian supermarket chain Pao de Acucar, formally known as Companhia Brasileira de Distribuicao, said it will invest 504 million reais ($479.4 million) through 1998 to expand and modernize its units.

Fully 260 million reais of the total investment plan will be invested this year and the remainder will be spent next year, Abilio Diniz, Pao de Acucar group president, told reporters at a news conference.

The investment plan will allow the company to increase the size of its distribution center in Sao Paulo to nearly 200,000 square meters, modernize its information network and improve logistics system.
Expansion of the distribution center is expected to be completed in August, Diniz said.

With the new distribution center, the company expects to be able to reduce stocks, increase the number of supermakets and cut costs. "Our investment is for infra-structure to provide clients better products with lower prices because costs will be lower," Diniz added.
The company plans to open this year seven supermarkets and 10 electrical appliance shops. In 1998, Diniz hopes to open another 19 units but he would not disclose how many supermarkets and shops.
The investment plan also includes remodelling of 80 supermarkets. Currently, Pao de Acucar has 223 units and 20,737 employees.
Under the inflation-adjusted accounting method, Pao de Acucar posted a net profit of 120.7 million reais in 1996, an increase of 57.6 percent over 1995, Diniz said.
He noted that Pao de Acucar invested 118 million reais and 226 million reais in 1995 and 1996, respectively.
